scope.focus_question: Given an unfamiliar study of evaluation awareness, decide what each measurement supports, diagnose a confound, and design a check that could change the conclusion.
scope.audience: ARENA applicant who reads research prose and wants independent practice interpreting an empirical paper.
outcomes: Explain phrase probability and verbalization with an original example.
Interpret the main figures and prompt-versus-rollout evidence.
Design matched, held-out and intervention tests that discriminate rival explanations.
Compute phrase probabilities, rollout summaries, pairwise AUROC and the chance of at least one flag.
Use a numerical result to explain what a reported experiment measures, with no requirement to implement or run an experiment.

inputs.include: Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appendices A–D

inputs.exclude: Prompt examples and operational attack details

inputs.include: Abstract and main results: decodability, verbalization and steering
Readout targets, grader effects and training-awareness control
Measurement, validity, related research and replication program
inputs.exclude: Application answer drafts and unverified comment-only details

inputs.include: Sections 4 and 5: ties in ROC paths and area-under-curve as a ranking statistic
inputs.exclude: Model fitting, ROC averaging and model comparison tooling

background.probe: Explain what changes between one success in ten trials and three successes in ten trials.

background.claim: Prior exposure to the Goodfire study
background.basis: Learner provided the paper and research report
background.probe: Explain why a model may score a phrase highly even if none of three sampled traces contains it.

scope.exclusions: Application submission prose, model execution and implementation, large-scale replication, and advanced experimental or ablation pipelines. Simple controls are considered when interpreting reported results.
scope.elicitation_notes: Primary sources and the supplied research guide. No expert interview, observed learner performance, or pilot.

evidence.question: aea-observe.signal.direct-1
evidence.observes: Sampling can miss an elevated but low-probability continuation. The evidence is for availability of the selected phrasing. Three draws can all omit the same phrase even when its probability is higher than a control.
evidence.warrant: The response applies this distinction to the given case: Distinguish a sampled continuation from the probability of an unsampled phrase.
evidence.rival: A memorized slogan can sound plausible without identifying the comparison in this case.

evidence.question: aea-observe.signal.direct-2

evidence.rival: A memorized slogan can sound plausible without identifying the comparison in this case.

dependencies.reason: A prompt maximum compares conditional phrase scores at different prefixes.
dependencies.counterfactual: Without a boundary score the learner cannot tell what each number in the max represents.

dependencies.reason: Figure 2 compares rankings induced by two different prompt scores at each budget.
dependencies.counterfactual: Without the aggregation rule the learner cannot identify which one-rollout score actually ranks the prompts.

dependencies.reason: Transport compares fixed score rankings and operating thresholds on distinct populations.
dependencies.counterfactual: Without interpreting a ranking statistic the learner cannot explain why AUROC can survive while a frozen threshold fails.

dependencies.reason: The task interprets an AUROC claim as a comparison of positive and negative items.
dependencies.counterfactual: Without pairwise scoring, the learner can mistake ranking for threshold accuracy.

dependencies.reason: The second part interprets the frequency of ever-positive prompts after increasing their sample budget.
dependencies.counterfactual: Without the complement relationship, the learner cannot explain why the observed group changes even when per-draw propensity is stable.

semantic_links.reason: Sampling can omit a phrase by chance, while faithfulness tests whether an omitted factor influenced a decision.
Grouping observed rollouts assesses association. Randomized interventions test effects on behavior.
A phrase readout is tied to linguistic expression, so different phrase targets can behave differently.
A source cue can remain predictive in a random split and fail on a different evaluation source.
A controlled behavior shift can support one link in a strategic account, while incentives and objective require separate evidence.
The variance comparison summarizes a per-rollout peak and groups traces by individual or prompt-level verbalization.
